prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier judging a wine recommender. A customer
with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Hi, I am looking for a sweet red wine that tastes like nuts."

The recommender suggested these 5 wines (described by a professional
tasting note):

Wine 1: Merlot, Italy, $460. Tasting note: "A perfect wine from a classic vintage, the 2007 Masseto (100% Merlot from a 17-acre vineyard of the same name) opens with an unabashedly opulent bouquet of delicious blackberry, cherry, chocolate, vanilla, exotic spice and cinnamon. Masseto excels both in terms of quality of fruit and winemaking and delivers plush, velvety tannins and an extra long, supple finish. It will make a special and valuable collection to your cellar."
Wine 2: Portuguese Red, Portugal, $450. Tasting note: "This is the latest release of what has long been regarded as Portugal's iconic wine. And it is magnificent. The last vintage was the 2004 and the wait has now shown to be worthwhile. With its immense span and breadth of flavors and rich structure it is a superb manifestation of the great vineyards of the Douro Superior. Big bold fruits and acidity are matched by the tannins and concentration. Hold this for many years or at least wait until 2022."
Wine 3: Sangiovese, Italy, $550. Tasting note: "This gorgeous, fragrant wine opens with classic Sangiovese scents of violet, rose, perfumed red berry, new leather and a whiff of baking spice. The elegant, radiant palate delivers crushed Marasca cherry, ripe strawberry, cinnamon, black tea and a hint of pipe tobacco. Firm, ultrafine tannins and bright acidity offer an age-worthy structure and impeccable balance. It's already stunning but will evolve for decades. Drink 2020–2050."
Wine 4: Cabernet Sauvignon, US, $200. Tasting note: "Tasted in a flight of great and famous Napa wines, this Cardinale stood at the head of the pack. Starts with a very fine nose of cedar, cassis, ripe blackberries and violets, then turns dramatic and refined in the mouth. Shows vast depth and length, with the finish a full minute of sweet fruits and spices. Marvelous tannins, so plush and elegant, so powerful yet refined. The grapes hail from Mt. Veeder, Howell Mountain, Stags Leap and Oakville, and the blend contains 14% Merlot. As good as it is now, it will improve for at least eight years."
Wine 5: Bordeaux-style Red Blend, France, $150. Tasting note: "This is a magnificently solid wine, initially even a bit severe. At this young stage, the tannins dominate, but it's also full of black fruit notes. Very dense and concentrated, this is a wine that's even better than the legendary 2005. The structure tells of its extraordinary aging potential: don't even attempt to drink this for 10 years."

Rate how well each wine matches the request, using this scale:
5 = matches every wish in the request
4 = matches the main wishes, misses a minor one
3 = partly matches: right kind of wine but several wishes missed, or the reverse
2 = matches only a small part of the request
1 = does not match (wrong kind of wine, or contradicts a wish)
Judge only from the information given. A wish the information cannot
confirm (for example a price that is unknown) is neither a match nor a
mismatch.

Then rate the set:
- set_relevance: how useful the 5 wines are together as an answer to the request (1-5).

Think briefly about each wine before scoring it. Answer with JSON only, in
this form:
{"wines": [{"reason": "<one sentence>", "relevance": <1-5>}, ... one per wine, in order],
 "set_relevance": <1-5>}
